question:
A tenant has lived in the same flat for thirty years, always under a lease and always treating the landlord as the owner. Can he acquire ownership of the flat by usucapión?
Options: yes / no.
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T19:concepts:2]
Módulo 1 · Tema 19: Possession (La Posesión) — Key concepts
- Classification axes: natural (mere corpus, no animus domini — e.g., a tenant) vs. civil possession (corpus + animus domini — leads to usucapión); as owner (generates legitimacy presumption, can lead to usucapión) vs. as holder/tenedor (acknowledges another's title — tenant, usufructuary, depositary — CANNOT acquire by usucapión); own name vs. another's name (representative, possession servant); immediate (direct) vs. mediate (through another — a landlord has mediate possession, the tenant has immediate possession); just (lawful acquisition) vs. unjust (violence, clandestinity, mere tolerance — merely tolerated acts create NO possession at all); good faith (unaware of a title defect) vs. bad faith (aware of the defect).

[en:M1:T17:concepts:8]
Módulo 1 · Tema 17: Real Property Rights (Derechos Reales) — Key concepts
- Usucapión (acquisitive prescription): ordinary (possession as owner, public/peaceful/uninterrupted + just title + good faith — 10 years between persons present / 20 years absent) vs. extraordinary (no good faith/title needed — 30 years of open, peaceful possession as owner suffices). Real risk on abandoned rural estates and unfenced plots — registry ownership is NOT a bar to usucapión by a possessor meeting the legal requirements.
- Modes of LOSING dominion: voluntary (alienation, abandonment) vs. involuntary (destruction of the thing, revocation — e.g., resolutory condition for non-payment, forced expropriation — requires prior justiprecio payment, original acquisition by a third party via usucapión).

[en:M1:T20:concepts:11]
Módulo 1 · Tema 20: Limited Real Rights — Usufruct, Surface Right, Air Rights, Easements — Key concepts
- **Usucapión of easements — critical restriction**: ONLY continuous AND apparent easements can be acquired by usucapión (20 years public/peaceful/uninterrupted possession, art. 537 CC). Discontinuous or non-apparent easements CANNOT be acquired this way — e.g., a right-of-way easement (discontinuous) is never usucapión-acquirable, only by title or "destination by the head of household" (art. 541 CC — an apparent sign between two same-owner estates becomes a title of easement when one estate transfers, unless removed/excluded beforehand).

[en:M1:T8:concepts:12]
Módulo 1 · Tema 8: Law 29/1994 on Urban Leases (LAU) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Other-use leases (Title III, arts. 29-35): mostly free agreement; art. 32 lets a business/professional tenant sublet/assign WITHOUT landlord consent (contrast with housing leases) but landlord gets a rent increase (10% partial sublease, 20% assignment/full sublease); art. 34 grants compensation to a retail tenant losing the premises after ≥5 years of activity provided the tenant stated, 4 months before expiry, the wish to renew for at least 5 more years at market rent; if the tenant reopens the same business in the same municipality within 6 months, compensation = moving costs + lost clientele; if not, and the landlord or a third party runs the same or a similar business there within 6 months, 1 month's rent per year of the lease (max. 18).

[en:M1:T19:vocab:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 19: Possession (La Posesión) — Spanish vocabulary
| posesión | possession |
| corpus / animus | material element / intentional element |
| animus domini | intent to hold as owner |
| posesión civilísima | civilísima (constructive/automatic) possession |
| poseedor de buena/mala fe | possessor in good/bad faith |
| frutos percibidos | fruits received |
| gastos necesarios / útiles / de lujo | necessary / useful / luxury expenses |
| derecho de retención | right of retention |
| interdicto posesorio | possessory injunction (historical term) |
| acción publiciana | Publician action |
| despojo | dispossession |
| tradición | delivery |
| tenedor | mere holder (non-owner possessor) |
answer: The tenant has had 30 years of continuous, peaceful possession as an owner (art. 537 CC), which qualifies for extraordinary usucapión (no good faith or title needed — 30 years of open, peaceful possession as owner suffices). However, the tenant is not the owner but a mere holder (tenedor), which prevents acquisition by usucapión. The tenant’s possession is not as owner but as holder, so even with 30 years, usucapión does not apply. Answer: no.

question:
Właściciel udzielił zlecenia (mandato) wynajęcia swojego mieszkania za nie mniej niż 1 200 € miesięcznie. Przyjmujący zlecenie podpisał umowę najmu za 900 € miesięcznie, a właściciel następnie potwierdził tę umowę na piśmie. Czy ta umowa najmu wiąże właściciela?
Opcje: tak / nie.
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[pl:M1:T15:concepts:6]
Módulo 1 · Tema 15: Umowy darowizny, pożyczki (Comodato/Mutuo) i zlecenia — Kluczowe pojęcia
- Zlecenie/mandato (art. 1709 CC): przyjmujący zlecenie (mandatario) zobowiązuje się działać za dającego zlecenie (mandante) — podstawa prawna działania API w imieniu klienta. Konsensualne, nieformalne (ale czynności rozporządzające, jak sprzedaż/hipoteka, wymagają WYRAŹNEGO zlecenia z wystarczającymi umocowaniami), domniemane jako NIEODPŁATNE, ale domniemane jako ODPŁATNE, gdy zawód przyjmującego polega na świadczeniu tego rodzaju usług (czyli agent nieruchomości) — korzystne domniemanie dla prawa API do wynagrodzenia. Intuitu personae — oparte na zaufaniu, wygasa ze śmiercią/utratą zdolności którejkolwiek strony.
- Zakres zlecenia: ogólne (tylko zwykły zarząd, czynności rozporządzające wymagają zlecenia wyraźnego) vs. szczególne (konkretne sprawy); przedstawicielskie (skutki spadają bezpośrednio na dającego zlecenie) vs. nieprzedstawicielskie (skutki najpierw u przyjmującego, który musi je przenieść).

[pl:M1:T16:concepts:4]
Módulo 1 · Tema 16: Pełnomocnictwo, negotiorum gestio, pośrednictwo i poręczenie — Kluczowe pojęcia
- Negotiorum gestio / gestión de negocios ajenos (art. 1888-1894 CC): osoba (prowadzący/gestor) dobrowolnie podejmuje się cudzych spraw (właściciela sprawy/dueño) BEZ zlecenia ani obowiązku ustawowego — quasi-kontraktowe źródło zobowiązań, zapobiega bezpodstawnemu wzbogaceniu. Wymogi: działanie w interesie właściciela (nie własnym), zgodne z prawem, brak wcześniejszego umocowania/zlecenia, dobrowolne, ze starannością rozsądnego gospodarza.
- **Obowiązek kontynuacji przez prowadzącego (art. 1888 CC)** — nie może jednostronnie porzucić prowadzenia sprawy raz rozpoczętego, jeśli właściciel poniósłby szkodę; musi kontynuować do zakończenia lub do czasu, aż właściciel sam może przejąć. Prowadzący odpowiada nawet za szkodę PRZYPADKOWĄ, jeśli podjął ryzykowne operacje, których właściciel normalnie nie prowadził, lub podporządkował interes właściciela własnemu. Obowiązek zwrotu przez właściciela zależy od RATYFIKACJI: przy ratyfikacji czynności stają się wiążące, jakby od początku istniało zlecenie; przy jej BRAKU właściciel zwraca tylko wydatki użyteczne/korzystne, do wysokości rzeczywistego wzbogacenia.

[pl:M1:T8:concepts:8]
Módulo 1 · Tema 8: Ley 29/1994 o najmie lokali miejskich (LAU) — tekst ustawy (źródło pierwotne) — Kluczowe pojęcia
- Kaucja / fianza (art. 36): OBOWIĄZKOWA — 1 miesięczny czynsz (mieszkania) lub 2 miesięczne czynsze (inne cele), w gotówce; nieaktualizowalna przez pierwsze 5/7 lat; dodatkowe zabezpieczenia ponad kaucję ograniczone do 2 miesięcznych czynszów dla najmu mieszkaniowego ≤5/7 lat (1 miesięczny czynsz przy najmie mieszkania czasowego), a od najemcy nigdy nie można wymagać ubezpieczenia od niepłacenia czynszu (art. 36.5 w brzmieniu RDL 29/2026, do zatwierdzenia przez Kongres). Po zakończeniu najmu obie strony muszą podpisać dokument stwierdzający stan mieszkania; jeśli go nie podpisano albo nie odnotowano w nim szkód, domniemywa się, że mieszkanie zwrócono w należytym stanie (art. 36.7). Niezwrócona kaucja jest oprocentowana odsetkami ustawowymi po upływie 1 miesiąca od zwrotu kluczy.

[pl:M1:T15:vocab:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 15: Umowy darowizny, pożyczki (Comodato/Mutuo) i zlecenia — Słownictwo hiszpańskie
| donación | darowizna |
| animus donandi | zamiar dokonania darowizny |
| donación inoficiosa | darowizna nieoficjozalna (przekraczająca część rozrządzalną) |
| donación con reversión | darowizna z klauzulą powrotu |
| donación modal / sub modo | darowizna z poleceniem |
| comodato / comodante / comodatario | użyczenie / użyczający / biorący w używanie |
| mutuo / mutuante / mutuatario | pożyczka na zużycie / pożyczkodawca / pożyczkobiorca |
| mandato / mandante / mandatario | zlecenie / dający zlecenie / przyjmujący zlecenie |
| rendición de cuentas | złożenie rachunków |
| revocación / renuncia | odwołanie / wypowiedzenie |
| FEIN / FIAE | standaryzowane formularze przedkontraktowej informacji kredytowej |
answer: Właściciel udzielił zlecenia (mandato) wynajęcia mieszkania, a przyjmujący zlecenie podpisał umowę najmu za 900 €, a właściciel potwierdził ją. Zgodnie z art. 1709 CC, zlecenie jest konsensualne i nieformalne, ale czynności rozporządzające (jak sprzedaż lub hipoteka) wymagają wyraźnego zlecenia z wystarczającymi umocowaniami. W tym przypadku umowa najmu to czynność rozporządzająca, więc musi być wyraźnie zapisana. Właściciel potwierdził umowę na piśmie, co świadczy o jej wyraźnym zleceniu. Zatem umowa najmu wiąże właściciela. Odpowiedź: tak.

question: Halfway through a ten-year rural lease in Málaga, the leased plot is reclassified as developable urban land. The landlord wants to end the lease on that ground. How many years' notice must the landlord give?
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T12:concepts:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 12: Law 49/2003 on Rural Leases (LAR) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Rural lease (art. 1): temporary transfer of one or more rural properties (or part) for agricultural, livestock, or forestry use in exchange for rent; agreement of the parties governs first, then the LAR, then supplementarily the CC/custom. Lease of a "holding" (explotación, art. 2) treats the whole organic productive unit as the object, with an inventory attached.
- Excluded from LAR (art. 6): seasonal leases under one agricultural year, land tilled/prepared at owner's expense for specified sowing, expropriated-for-public-utility properties, secondary uses (stubble grazing, montanera, hunting, fallow improvement), industrial livestock operations, communal/local-corporation property and montes vecinales en mano común.
- Non-application (art. 7): LAU-scope leases, or properties that are urban/developable land, or where non-rural income exceeds double the rural income — landlord can then terminate with 1 year's notice if this arises mid-contract.

[en:M1:T8:concepts:4]
Módulo 1 · Tema 8: Law 29/1994 on Urban Leases (LAU) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Tacit extension (art. 10): after the 5/7-year minimum, if neither party gives notice (landlord: 4 months; tenant: 2 months before expiry), contract extends annually up to 3 more years. Extraordinary extensions exist for vulnerable tenants (1 year, mandatory if landlord is a "gran tenedor"/large-scale holder) and for stressed-market-area dwellings (up to 3 more years, mandatory unless specific exceptions). Temporary rule (RDL 29/2026, pending validation by Congress, DF 5ª): for habitual-residence leases in force on 8 Oct 2026 whose compulsory extension ends before 31 Dec 2028, or whose tacit extension ends, the tenant may ask for up to 2 more years in annual periods if the rent has been paid on time for the previous 8 months; the landlord must accept unless the parties agree otherwise, sign a new lease, or the landlord proves a real need to occupy the dwelling (art. 9.3); it does not apply where a renewal at least 5% cheaper is agreed.

[en:M1:T13:concepts:2]
Módulo 1 · Tema 13: Rustic Properties — Course Module on the LAR (Condensed Practitioner View) — Key concepts
- Minor as landlord: property must be leased on their behalf by parental-authority holders/guardian; once emancipated, the minor can end the lease after the 5-year minimum term has run, by notifying the tenant within 6 months of emancipation (or of the date when 1 year of the minimum term remains); the termination takes effect only 1 year after it is given (art. 9.4 LAR).
- Landlord's core obligations: deliver property fit for agreed use; maintain tenant in peaceful/useful possession (liable for eviction and latent defects); necessary works/repairs at no rent increase; force-majeure exception (non-compensable damage costing more than 1 year's rent → landlord not obliged to repair, tenant chooses rescission or continuation with reduced rent); bear legally/judicially mandated improvement works.

[en:M1:T9:citations:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 9: The Lease Contract — Course Module on the LAU (Condensed Practitioner View) — Key citations
- Law 4/2013, RDL 7/2019, Law 12/2023 — successive LAU reforms (3yr → 5/7yr minimum term → stressed areas/gran tenedor).
- Art. 5(e) LAU — VUT exclusion from LAU scope, governed by regional tourism rules.
- Art. 36 LAU + regional decrees — deposit lodging obligation with the regional housing body.

[en:M1:T12:vocab:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 12: Law 49/2003 on Rural Leases (LAR) — Primary Legislative Text — Spanish vocabulary
| arrendamiento rústico | rural/agricultural lease |
| finca rústica | rustic property |
| explotación agraria | agricultural holding |
| agricultor profesional | professional farmer |
| IPREM | Public Multiple-Purpose Income Indicator |
| aparcería | sharecropping |
| tanteo y retracto | right of first refusal and redemption |
| retracto de colindantes | adjoining-owner redemption right |
| enervación | curing (default) to stay an eviction |
| montanera | acorn/mast grazing |
| montes vecinales en mano común | neighborhood commons |
| premio de afección | affection premium (expropriation surcharge) |
answer: The lease is under the LAR, but the property is now urban/developable, so it falls outside LAR scope (art. 7). Under LAU, the landlord can terminate with 1 year's notice if the property is urban/developable (art. 7). Answer: 1 year.

question:
Our owners' community in Spain wants to claim unpaid community fees from the registered owner of one of the flats. Which special court procedure can the community use for this claim?
Options: arbitration / juicio ordinario / proceso monitorio / juicio verbal.
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T10:concepts:7]
Módulo 1 · Tema 10: Law 49/1960 on Horizontal Property (LPH) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Debt collection: community can use the special "proceso monitorio" (payment-order) procedure against the registered owner; if the debtor opposes, the community may request a precautionary attachment, which the court grants without the community posting security (art. 21.4).
- Extinction of horizontal property (art. 23): destruction of the building (presumed when reconstruction cost exceeds 50% of the property's value, unless insurance covers the excess), or conversion to ordinary co-ownership.
- Private real-estate complexes / urbanizaciones (art. 24): 2+ independent buildings/plots sharing indivisible co-ownership of common elements (roads, installations); may constitute as a single community (fully subject to LPH) or as a grouping/federation of communities (agrupación de comunidades) with its own president-based Assembly and quota system, competence limited to shared elements only.

[en:M1:T11:concepts:4]
Módulo 1 · Tema 11: Horizontal Property — Course Module (Condensed Practitioner View) — Key concepts
- Debt-collection payment-order procedure (proceso monitorio): the initial petition needs no lawyer or procurador whatever the amount (art. 814.2 LEC); if the debtor opposes, they are needed once the claim exceeds €2,000 (arts. 23, 31 and 818 LEC). File with the Court of First Instance: (1) the certificate of the assembly's debt-liquidation resolution, issued by the secretary with the president's approval and stating the amount and its breakdown, and (2) proof that the debt was notified to the debtor (or posted on the community notice board for at least 3 days) (art. 21.3 LPH). If the debtor neither pays nor opposes within 20 days, the monitorio ends and execution is issued on the community's request; suing the registered owner lets the execution reach the flat (art. 816 LEC, art. 21.2 LPH).

[en:M1:T23:concepts:4]
Módulo 1 · Tema 23: Mortgage/Registry Law — The Registral Property, First Registration, and Cadastre Coordination — Key concepts
- Area surplus/exceso de cabida (real area > registered) vs. shortfall/defecto de cabida (real < registered) — Law 13/2015 completely reformed this: **an area difference of up to 10% can be registered without a proceeding when the descriptive and graphic cadastral certificate (CCDG) shows the parcel fully matching the registered plot, and up to 5% even without it (art. 201.3 LH) — but only if the registrar, in a reasoned decision, has no grounded doubts (e.g. the area was measured exactly before, repeated rectifications, or the plot came from a segregation, division or aggregation); after registering, the registrar notifies the registered owners of the adjoining plots**; surpluses >10% require the full art. 199 or art. 201 LH procedure with adjoining-owner notice. DGSJFP doctrine: area surplus is ONLY for correcting a measurement error on an already-registered property — NEVER a disguised way to register additional/unregistered land.

[en:M1:T10:concepts:4]
Módulo 1 · Tema 10: Law 49/1960 on Horizontal Property (LPH) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Governing bodies (art. 13): Assembly of owners, President (+ optional Vice-Presidents), Secretary, Administrator — secretary/administrator roles can be combined with presidency or separated; terms default to 1 year unless bylaws say otherwise.

[en:M1:T10:vocab:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 10: Law 49/1960 on Horizontal Property (LPH) — Primary Legislative Text — Spanish vocabulary
| propiedad horizontal | horizontal property / condominium regime |
| elementos comunes / privativos | common / private elements |
| cuota de participación | participation quota |
| título constitutivo | title deed (constituting the regime) |
| estatutos | community bylaws |
| junta de propietarios | assembly of owners |
| fondo de reserva | reserve fund |
| afección real | real charge (debt attaching to the property) |
| certificado de deudas | certificate of community debts |
| proceso monitorio | payment-order (summary debt) procedure |
| impugnación de acuerdos | challenging assembly resolutions |
| complejo inmobiliario privado | private real-estate complex |
| VUT (vivienda de uso turístico) | tourist-use dwelling |
answer: The community can use the "proceso monitorio" (payment-order) procedure against the registered owner. This is a special court procedure for debt collection in horizontal property matters. The community can initiate the process without a lawyer or procurador, and if the debtor opposes, they must be notified. The procedure is governed by art. 814.2 LEC and art. 21.2 LPH. Answer: proceso monitorio.

question: Osoba fizyczna zaciągnęła w 2024 r. kredyt hipoteczny na swoje mieszkanie ze zwykłą stopą odsetek 3%. Spóźnia się z ratą. Jaka stopa odsetek za opóźnienie, w procentach rocznie, ma zastosowanie do zaległej kwoty?
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[pl:M2:T20:concepts:2]
Módulo 2 · Tema 20: Kalkulacja handlowa i finansowa — Kluczowe pojęcia
- Ustawowa stopa odsetek pieniężnych ustalana jest corocznie w hiszpańskiej ustawie budżetowej; przy opóźnieniu w zapłacie długu pieniężnego (art. 1108 CC) należą się odsetki umowne, a w ich braku — ustawowe; od wyroku pierwszej instancji zasądzającego zapłatę: odsetki ustawowe + 2 punkty (art. 576 LEC); przy hipotecznych kredytach mieszkaniowych dla osób fizycznych zawartych od 16 czerwca 2019 r.: odsetki za opóźnienie = stopa odsetek zwykłych + 3 punkty, tylko od kwoty zaległej i nigdy nie kapitalizowane (art. 25 LCCI 5/2019).
- Systemy amortyzacji: francuski (stała rata, najczęstszy w hipotekach), niemiecki (stała rata kapitałowa, malejąca rata łączna), amerykański/bullet (tylko odsetki, kapitał na koniec).
- Zastaw papierów wartościowych (loan-to-value 40–70%) pozwala inwestorowi uzyskać płynność bez sprzedaży aktywów i bez wywoływania zysku/straty kapitałowej dla IRPF.

[pl:M2:T21:concepts:3]
Módulo 2 · Tema 21: Kredyty i systemy amortyzacji — Kluczowe pojęcia
- Im dłuższy okres amortyzacji → niższa rata miesięczna, ale WIĘCEJ łącznych odsetek; stopa procentowa ma większy wpływ na koszt niż okres.
- System francuski: rata stała, część odsetkowa maleje, a kapitałowa rośnie w czasie (raty kapitałowe tworzą postęp geometryczny o ilorazie (1+i)). System niemiecki: rata kapitałowa stała, rata łączna maleje, łączny koszt odsetek jest NIŻSZY niż we francuskim. System amerykański: tylko odsetki, kapitał na koniec, często łączony z funduszem umorzeniowym.
- Karencja (płacone tylko odsetki, bez amortyzacji kapitału) obniża początkową ratę, ale podnosi łączne odsetki i ratę po karencji — zalecana tylko przy udokumentowanych przejściowych trudnościach lub kredytach deweloperskich w trakcie budowy.

[pl:M2:T20:citations:1]
Módulo 2 · Tema 20: Kalkulacja handlowa i finansowa — Kluczowe przepisy
- Art. 1108 Código Civil — opóźnienie w zapłacie: odsetki umowne, a w ich braku ustawowe. Art. 576 LEC — od wyroku zasądzającego zapłatę: odsetki ustawowe + 2 punkty (odsetki procesowe).
- Ley 5/2019 (LCCI) — obowiązkowe ujawnienie TAE; odsetki za opóźnienie przy hipotekach = stopa zwykła + 3 punkty, tylko od kwot zaległych, bez kapitalizacji (art. 25; kredyty od 16 czerwca 2019 r.); progi przedterminowej wymagalności + wezwanie z miesięcznym terminem (art. 24)

- Circular 5/2012 Banco de España (wielokrotnie zmieniana, ostatnio przez Circular 3/2022) — metodologia obliczania TAE
- Ley 3/2004 — opóźnienia w płatnościach w transakcjach handlowych, stopa = stopa EBC + 8 punktów

- Odsetki proste: `I = Co · i · n`; Kapitał końcowy: `Cn = Co · (1 + i·n)`
- Kapitał końcowy przy oprocentowaniu składanym: `Cn = Co · (1 + i)ⁿ`; Wartość bieżąca przy oprocentowaniu składanym: `Co = Cn·(1+i)⁻ⁿ`

question: A widow aged 60 inherits the life usufruct of her late husband's flat. Under the state Inheritance and Gift Tax rules, what percentage of the flat's total value is the usufruct worth?

Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T14:concepts:6]
Módulo 1 · Tema 14: Law 29/1987 on Inheritance and Gift Tax (ISD) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- **Multiplying coefficients by pre-existing wealth + kinship group (art. 22)** — this is what makes the tax dramatically higher for distant/unrelated heirs: coefficients range from 1.0000 (Groups I/II, wealth ≤€402,678.11) up to 2.4000 (Group IV, wealth >€4,020,770.98) — Group IV pays roughly DOUBLE the base tax liability compared to close relatives even at the lowest wealth bracket (2.0000 vs 1.0000).
- Usufruct valuation (art. 26): temporary usufruct = 2% of total value per year (capped 70%); life usufruct = 70% minus 1% per year of usufructuary's age above 19 (minimum 10%). Bare ownership value = total value minus usufruct value.
- Accrual (art. 24): mortis causa tax accrues on date of death (or final declaration of absence); inter vivos gifts accrue on the date of the act/contract. Suspended-effect acquisitions (condition/term/trust) accrue when the limitation ceases.

[en:M6:T46:concepts:7]
Módulo 6 · Tema 46: Cost or Replacement Method — Key concepts
- **Valuation of real rights** (also in this tema): a real right reduces an asset's value — `asset value = total value − real right value`. - **Life usufruct**: `% = 89 − age of usufructuary` (min 10%, max 70%). - **Temporary usufruct**: `% = 2 × years of duration` (max 70%). - **Bare ownership** = total value − usufruct value. - **Use and habitation** = 75% of the corresponding usufruct value. - **Easements**: value = (property value free of the easement) − (property value burdened by it); same subtraction logic applies to most other unregulated real rights/restrictions.

[en:M1:T20:concepts:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 20: Limited Real Rights — Usufruct, Surface Right, Air Rights, Easements — Key concepts
- Usufruct (art. 467 CC, arts. 467-522): a real right to enjoy another's property with the obligation to preserve its FORM and SUBSTANCE, unless the constituting title or law authorizes otherwise. Limited real right (ius in re aliena), erga omnes, temporary by nature (max. 30 years if usufructuary is a legal person — never perpetual), transferable/mortgageable EXCEPT most legal usufructs, registrable in the Land Registry for third-party effect.
- **Tax valuation of usufruct — memorize this formula**: life usufruct value = 89% minus the usufructuary's age (minimum 10%) of the asset's value; bare ownership = the complement up to 100% (based on ISD Law 29/1987 art. 26). "Usufruct with power of disposal" (usufructuario con facultad de disponer) can be treated by tax authorities as a FULL transmission for ISD purposes if the usufructuary can freely alienate.

[en:M1:T15:concepts:5]
Módulo 1 · Tema 15: Gift, Loan (Comodato/Mutuo), and Mandate Contracts — Key concepts
- Gift tax treatment: donee is the ISD taxpayer (not the donor); donor may still owe IRPF on any capital gain if the gift's value exceeds acquisition cost (no reinvestment exemption for gifts, unlike a sale of primary residence); a private gift is not subject to VAT (business/professional gifts of business assets can trigger self-consumption VAT); ISD filing deadline = 30 BUSINESS days from the day after the gift date. question:
A baby in Madrid is stillborn, never showing any sign of life. Did the baby acquire legal personality under the Civil Code?
Options: no / yes.
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T1:concepts:2]
Módulo 1 · Tema 1: Concept of Law. Civil, Commercial and Regional (Foral) Law — Key concepts
- Civil Code (Código Civil, CC): published by Royal Decree of 24 July 1889 (NOT 6 Oct 1888 — that was a superseded first edition; exam trap). Structure: Preliminary Title (arts. 1–16) + 4 Books — I Persons, II Property/ownership, III Modes of acquiring ownership, IV Obligations and contracts.
- Key special civil laws outside the CC: LPH (Law 49/1960, horizontal property), LAU (Law 29/1994, urban leases), Mortgage Law (1946), LOE (Law 38/1999, building regulation), LCCI (Law 5/2019, real estate credit), Law 12/2023 (Right to Housing).
- Commercial Law governs businesspeople (empresarios) and businesses (empresas); based on Commercial Code of 1885 (4 books) and Capital Companies Act (RDL 1/2010).

[en:M1:T2:concepts:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 2: The Subject of the Legal Relationship — Key concepts
- Legal relationship = normative bond between subjects of law (never solely between things); three elements: subjects (active = rights holders, passive = duty holders), object, and content (rights + duties).
- Person (Albaladejo): every being the law accepts as capable of rights and obligations. Distinguish **person** (the being) from **legal personality** (the quality/fitness of being a subject of rights and obligations) — "one IS a person, one HAS legal personality."
- Legal personality begins at birth: art. 30 CC (as reformed by Law 20/2011) now requires only (1) live birth and (2) complete detachment from the mother's womb — the old requirement of "living 24 hours + human form" was abolished. Exam trap: know this is a changed rule.

[en:M1:T4:concepts:6]
Módulo 1 · Tema 4: The Legal Transaction (Negocio Jurídico) — Key concepts
- Actions that never prescribe: between co-heirs, co-owners or adjoining owners, the action to partition an inheritance, divide co-owned property or demarcate boundaries (deslinde) (art. 1965 CC); by doctrine and case law (not art. 1965) also personality/family/civil-status rights and the action for absolute nullity.
- Representation: legal (patria potestad, tutela, curatela representativa, defensor judicial — closed list) vs. voluntary (power of attorney/poder). Direct representation (effects fall on the represented person) is standard in real estate practice; requires contemplatio domini (acting visibly on behalf of another).
- Power of attorney types: general (broad, excludes strictly personal acts) vs. special (specific act, e.g. sell a named property — standard in real estate) vs. preventive power of attorney (poder preventivo, arts. 256–259 CC, Law 8/2021) — lets a person appoint an attorney-in-fact in advance for loss of capacity; notarized deed; avoids judicial incapacitation.

[en:M1:T20:concepts:11]
Módulo 1 · Tema 20: Limited Real Rights — Usufruct, Surface Right, Air Rights, Easements — Key concepts
- **Usucapión of easements — critical restriction**: ONLY continuous AND apparent easements can be acquired by usucapión (20 years public/peaceful/uninterrupted possession, art. 537 CC). Discontinuous or non-apparent easements CANNOT be acquired this way — e.g., a right-of-way easement (discontinuous) is never usucapión-acquirable, only by title or "destination by the head of household" (art. 541 CC — an apparent sign between two same-owner estates becomes a title of easement when one estate transfers, unless removed/excluded beforehand).

[en:M1:T1:vocab:1]

question:

[en:M1:T22:concepts:5]
Módulo 1 · Tema 22: The Land Registry (Registro de la Propiedad) — Key concepts
- (cont.) Imprescriptibility: acquisitive aspect (art. 35 LH — registration = just title, presumes public/peaceful/uninterrupted good-faith possession throughout the entry's term, protecting the registered owner from later-discovered original inaccuracy); extinctive aspect (Registry does NOT protect against a lapsed right — e.g. an unexercised 20-year mortgage action still prescribes); the action to RECTIFY the Registry itself is imprescriptible (art. 40 LH). 5. Specificity/especialidad (art. 9 LH): each entry must precisely identify the property, right, titleholder, and (for mortgages) the maximum secured amount — no generic/indefinite registrations, no general mortgage over all assets. 6. Application/rogación (art. 6 LH): the Registrar acts only on request — never ex officio (exceptions: e.g. Cadastre-coordination notes; even the lapse cancellation of an old mortgage under art. 82 LH needs a request from the holder of a registered right).

[en:M1:T23:concepts:4]

DGSJFP doctrine: area surplus is ONLY for correcting a measurement error on an already-registered property — NEVER a disguised way to register additional/unregistered land.

[en:M1:T4:concepts:5]
Módulo 1 · Tema 4: The Legal Transaction (Negocio Jurídico) — Key concepts

- LPH develops art. 396 CC (horizontal property/condominium). Each flat/unit carries a DUAL right (art. 3): (a) exclusive individual ownership of the private space + elements serving it exclusively, and (b) co-ownership of common elements — these two rights are inseparably united, cannot be sold apart from each other.
- Participation quota (cuota de participación, art. 5): assigned in the title deed based on useful floor area, location, and presumed use of common elements; expressed in hundredths of the building's total value; serves as the module for both charges and benefits. Improvements/impairments to a unit do NOT change its quota (only changeable per arts. 10 and 17 procedures).

- Debt-collection payment-order procedure (proceso monitorio): the initial petition needs no lawyer or procurador whatever the amount (art. 814.2 LEC); if the debtor opposes, they are needed once the claim exceeds €2,000 (arts. 23, 31 and 818 LEC). question:
A father gifted his eldest son a house worth far more than he could have left him by will, exceeding the freely disposable share. After the father's death, who can have the excess of that gift reduced?
Options: the donee / the father's creditors / the notary / the forced heirs.
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T15:concepts:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 15: Gift, Loan (Comodato/Mutuo), and Mandate Contracts — Key concepts
- Gift/donación (art. 618 CC): gratuitous act of liberality, donor disposes of a thing, donee accepts. Perfected when the DONOR becomes aware of the donee's acceptance (not when the donee accepts) — if donor dies before learning of acceptance, the gift has no effect. Characteristics: gratuitous, requires animus donandi (intent to enrich), consensual (delivery needed for consummation, not perfection), irrevocable in principle (only 3 exhaustive statutory grounds), a named contract (arts. 618-656 CC).
- Real element limits on gifting: donor must reserve what's needed to live on (else the gift is rescindable); quantitative cap — cannot give by gift more than could be given by will (excess = inofficious gift, donación inoficiosa, reducible by forced heirs after death); cannot gift FUTURE assets (art. 635 CC).

[en:M1:T18:concepts:2]
Módulo 1 · Tema 18: Co-ownership (Comunidad de Bienes) — Key concepts
- Structure types: Roman-type (by shares — CC's default/presumed model — each co-owner freely disposes of their OWN share without others' consent, any co-owner can demand division) vs. Germanic-type (joint hand/gesamte Hand — no individual disposable shares, only joint action — used for communal mountain land, water communities, and partly for gananciales marital property).
- Co-ownership vs. civil partnership (sociedad civil) — key distinctions: co-ownership can arise WITHOUT a prior agreement of wills (forced by law); a partnership always requires a contract. Co-ownership contributions are limited to assets (not labor/money alone, strictly); partnership contributions can be assets, money, OR labor/industry. Co-ownership has no profit purpose necessarily; partnership is profit-driven. Division: co-ownership divisible at will anytime (imprescriptible); a partner cannot unilaterally dissolve except for legal/agreed causes.

[en:M1:T19:concepts:9]
Módulo 1 · Tema 19: Possession (La Posesión) — Key concepts
- Loss of possession (art. 460 CC): voluntary (unequivocal abandonment — never presumed; transfer for onerous or gratuitous title with delivery) vs. involuntary (destruction/total loss of the thing; the thing falling outside commerce — e.g. expropriation into public domain; **possession by another for MORE THAN A YEAR, even against the former possessor's will** — this ties directly to the 1-year limitation period for possessory actions, art. 1968.1 CC and art. 439.1 LEC).

[en:M1:T14:concepts:7]
Módulo 1 · Tema 14: Law 29/1987 on Inheritance and Gift Tax (ISD) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Accumulation rule (art. 30): gifts between the SAME donor-donee within 3 years are treated as a single transfer for tax-rate purposes (average-rate mechanism) — an anti-fragmentation rule agents must flag for clients doing staged property gifts.
- Formal control mechanism (art. 33): documents evidencing a taxable ISD act CANNOT be registered/take effect in public offices or registries (including the Land Registry) unless proof of tax assessment submission is shown — critical for agents: an inherited/gifted property cannot be registered without first dealing with ISD. The Registry likewise will not register a transfer that triggers municipal plusvalía (IIVTNU) until the plusvalía return, or the communication under art. 110.6.b TRLRHL, has been filed (art. 254.5 LH).

The forced heirs have the right to claim the excess from the gift. Answer: the forced heirs.

question: My registered plot in Spain turns out to be bigger than the Land Registry records. I have no cadastral graphic description that fully matches the plot, but the registrar has no grounded doubts. retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T23:concepts:4]
Módulo 1 · Tema 23: Mortgage/Registry Law — The Registral Property, First Registration, and Cadastre Coordination — Key concepts
- Area surplus/exceso de cabida (real area > registered) vs. shortfall/defecto de cabida (real < registered) — Law 13/2015 completely reformed this: **an area difference of up to 10% can be registered without a proceeding when the descriptive and graphic cadastral certificate (CCDG) shows the parcel fully matching the registered plot, and up to 5% even without it (art. 201.3 LH) — but only if the registrar, in a reasoned decision, has no grounded doubts (e.g. the area was measured exactly before, repeated rectifications, or the plot came from a segregation, division or aggregation); after registering, the registrar notifies the registered owners of the adjoining plots**; surpluses >10% require the full art. 199 or art. 201 LH procedure with adjoining-owner notice. DGSJFP doctrine: area surplus is ONLY for correcting a measurement error on an already-registered property — NEVER a disguised way to register additional/unregistered land.

[en:M1:T23:citations:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 23: Mortgage/Registry Law — The Registral Property, First Registration, and Cadastre Coordination — Key citations
- Art. 9 LH (as amended by Law 13/2015) — property description requirements, cadastral reference, georeferencing.

- Art. 205 LH — first registration by double public title (minimum 1-year gap between titles).
- Art. 201.3 LH — area differences up to 10% with a fully matching CCDG (up to 5% without it) registrable without a proceeding, unless the registrar has grounded doubts; adjoining owners notified afterwards.
- Art. 199 vs. art. 201 LH — registral vs. notarial rectification procedures.
- Art. 208 LH — notarial proceeding to resume a genuinely interrupted chain of title; rule 1: acquiring directly from the registered owner or the owner's heirs is not an interruption.
- Art. 10.5 LH — presumption of coincidence for Registry-Cadastre coordinated properties.

[en:M1:T23:concepts:2]

question: Quiero construir un hotel rural en suelo rústico en Andalucía como actuación extraordinaria. El presupuesto de ejecución material es de 939.000 euros, de los que 143.000 euros son maquinaria. ¿Qué prestación compensatoria fija la LISTA?

Retrieved context:
[en:M3:T42:concepts:3]
Módulo 3 · Tema 42: Urban Planning Instruments (Módulo 31) — Key concepts
- Modification (partial, doesn't touch the territorial model) vs. Revision (overall reconsideration, replaces the model) of plans — revision needs the full original approval procedure including strategic environmental assessment.
- Public Interest Actions (AIP) on rustic land: exceptional authorization for non-agricultural uses (rural hotels, golf courses, energy plants) needing public-utility justification, siting necessity, landscape compatibility, and payment of a compensatory levy — in Andalusia, LISTA (in force 23 Dec 2021) replaced AIPs with 'extraordinary actions' (actuaciones extraordinarias) on rustic land, which need a prior authorisation before the licence (6 months to decide, silence = refusal) and a compensatory payment of 10% of the material execution budget of the works, excluding machinery (reducible by regulation) (art. 22 LISTA) — independent of the building permit and opening/activity permit.

[en:M2:T26:concepts:1]
Módulo 2 · Tema 26: Construction and Physical Elements — Key concepts
- A solar (buildable plot) requires 3 basic services: vehicle access, water supply + drainage, electricity supply; technically it must front a paved/lit road with alignments and grading marked, and building consolidated on ≥2/3 of buildable area also counts as urban land.
- Spanish land classification (tripartite, since the 1956 Ley del Suelo, now delegated to each Autonomous Community): suelo urbano (already serviced/developed), suelo urbanizable (developable, planned for future transformation), suelo no urbanizable/rústico (protected from construction — agricultural/forestry/environmental value). In Andalusia (Costa del Sol), LISTA (Ley 7/2021) replaced this with two classes only, suelo urbano and suelo rústico (art. 12); there is no suelo urbanizable. Nationally, RDLeg 7/2015 (TRLSRU) only distinguishes "rural land" vs "developed/urbanized land" (art. 21) for valuation/expropriation purposes.

[en:M3:T40:concepts:3]
Módulo 3 · Tema 40: Consolidated Land and Urban Rehabilitation Act (RDLeg. 7/2015) — Full Text — Key concepts
- Reversion vs. re-assessment (art. 47): reversion applies if the expropriation's use changes UNLESS (a) public-facility use maintained 8+ years, (b) land holdings expansion, (c) urban development action, (d) owner's own duty-failure caused the expropriation. For development-action expropriations specifically: reversion after 10 years without completed development; re-assessment (retasación) if use/floor-area changes increase value outside a full planning review.
- Compensable cases (art. 48): change in execution conditions before deadlines expire (or after, if delay is the Administration's fault); non-compensability applies to mere non-conformity-with-planning situations (fuera de ordenación) arising from later plan changes.
- Compulsory sale/substitution (arts. 49–50): triggered by an owner's failure to fulfil duties (build/conserve); awarded via publicity + competitive bidding; the content of ownership can never be reduced by more than 50% of its value.

Módulo 2 · Tema 26: Construction and Physical Elements — Key citations

- Real Decreto Legislativo 7/2015 (TRLSRU) — current national land law, "rural" vs "developed" basic situations (art. 21)

question:
I own a flat in a community of owners and want to let it as a tourist-use dwelling (VUT). What majority does the owners' meeting need to give me the prior approval?

- VUT approval within a community (art. 7.3 + 17.12): an owner wanting to run a tourist-use dwelling needs the community's EXPRESS prior approval by 3/5 majority; the community can also approve/restrict/prohibit such activity and set special expense quotas (increase capped at 20%, non-retroactive).

[en:M1:T10:concepts:5]
Módulo 1 · Tema 10: Law 49/1960 on Horizontal Property (LPH) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- **Voting majority thresholds — a key exam area (art. 17)**: - 1/3 owners + 1/3 quotas: telecom infrastructure, renewable-energy/new-supply infrastructure installation (non-consenting owners can't be charged unless they later opt in). - Simple majority (majority of owners + majority of quotas): accessibility works/lift installation (mandatory to pay even beyond 12 months' ordinary fees once approved) — and NO vote is needed when owners in whose unit a person with a disability or over 70 lives or works request them, if the annual cost passed on after subsidies is at most 12 months' ordinary fees, or if the requesters pay the excess (art. 10.1.b); energy-efficiency works (if annual cost after subsidies ≤12 monthly instalments — dissenters can't opt out here either). - 3/5 owners + 3/5 quotas: establishing/discontinuing concierge/security services; leasing unassigned common elements; non-required innovations/improvements above 3 months' ordinary fees (dissenters NOT bound, can opt in later by paying updated cost); physical division/merger/segregation of units, new floors, structural alterations; approving/restricting/prohibiting tourist-use (VUT) activity in a unit. - Unanimity: any resolution amending the title deed or bylaws not otherwise covered. - Ordinary/other resolutions: majority of ALL owners representing a majority of ALL quotas on first call; on second call, a majority of those present representing more than half of the quotas of those present (art. 17.7). - Silence rule (art. 17.8): absent owners duly summoned are counted as voting IN FAVOR if they don't object in writing within 30 calendar days of being informed of the resolution (except where cost can't be passed on to dissenters, or private-use modifications).

question:
At the owners' meeting a resolution was passed that causes one owner serious financial harm she has no legal duty to bear. She voted against it and is up to date with her community fees. How long does she have to challenge the resolution in court?

Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T10:concepts:6]
Módulo 1 · Tema 10: Law 49/1960 on Horizontal Property (LPH) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Owners not up to date on community debts (and not having judicially challenged or deposited the amount) may attend the Assembly but CANNOT VOTE (art. 15.2) — recorded in the minutes, excluded from majority calculations.
- Challenging Assembly resolutions (art. 18): grounds — contrary to law/bylaws, seriously prejudicial to the community for one owner's benefit, serious harm to an owner with no legal duty to bear it, or abuse of right. Standing: owners who voted against, absentees, and those improperly denied a vote — but the challenger must be current on community debts (or deposit them) to have standing (exception: challenges about quota-setting). **Deadline: 3 months generally, 1 year for resolutions contrary to law/bylaws.**

[en:M1:T10:concepts:5]
Módulo 1 · Tema 10: Law 49/1960 on Horizontal Property (LPH) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- **Voting majority thresholds — a key exam area (art. 17)**: - 1/3 owners + 1/3 quotas: telecom infrastructure, renewable-energy/new-supply infrastructure installation (non-consenting owners can't be charged unless they later opt in). - Simple majority (majority of owners + majority of quotas): accessibility works/lift installation (mandatory to pay even beyond 12 months' ordinary fees once approved) — and NO vote is needed when owners in whose unit a person with a disability or over 70 lives or works request them, if the annual cost passed on after subsidies is at most 12 months' ordinary fees, or if the requesters pay the excess (art. 10.1.b); energy-efficiency works (if annual cost after subsidies ≤12 monthly instalments — dissenters can't opt out here either). - 3/5 owners + 3/5 quotas: establishing/discontinuing concierge/security services; leasing unassigned common elements; non-required innovations/improvements above 3 months' ordinary fees (dissenters NOT bound, can opt in later by paying updated cost); physical division/merger/segregation of units, new floors, structural alterations; approving/restricting/prohibiting tourist-use (VUT) activity in a unit. - Unanimity: any resolution amending the title deed or bylaws not otherwise covered. - Ordinary/other resolutions: majority of ALL owners representing a majority of ALL quotas on first call; on second call, a majority of those present representing more than half of the quotas of those present (art. 17.7). - Silence rule (art. 17.8): absent owners duly summoned are counted as voting IN FAVOR if they don't object in writing within 30 calendar days of being informed of the resolution (except where cost can't be passed on to dissenters, or private-use modifications).

question:
This year my community voted a special, higher expense quota for my tourist-use flat. Can they also charge me that higher quota for the previous years in which I was already letting it?
Options: no / yes.
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T10:concepts:3]
Módulo 1 · Tema 10: Law 49/1960 on Horizontal Property (LPH) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- **Community debt real charge (afección real)**: unpaid community expenses attach to the flat/unit — a buyer is liable, WITH the property itself, for the previous owners' unpaid community debts for the part of the current year already due + the 3 preceding calendar years (art. 9.1.e); the seller must declare being up-to-date (or state what's owed) in the sale deed and provide a certificate of debts, without which the notary cannot authorize the deed (unless the buyer expressly waives this) — critical agent due-diligence checkpoint. Community debt claims for these periods are PREFERENTIAL: they rank ahead of a registered mortgage and registered attachments (art. 1923.3º–5º CC), but not ahead of the last year's taxes on the property or insurance premiums (art. 1923.1º–2º), and wage claims keep their preference.

[en:M4:T7:concepts:6]
Módulo 4 · Tema 7: Real Estate Taxation under Personal Income Tax (IRPF) and Corporate Income Tax (IS) — Key concepts
- **Special regime for residential-letting entities** (arts. 48-49 LIS): **40% relief** on the gross IS liability for qualifying rental income (85% until 2021; cut to 40% for tax periods from 1 January 2022 by Law 22/2021, art. 61.4) → at the 25% rate, an effective **15%**; requires ≥8 homes let/offered, minimum 3-year holding per unit, separate accounting, election notified to AEAT.
- **SOCIMIs** (Law 11/2009): 0% IS rate, but a special levy on undistributed profits that were not taxed at the general rate: 15%, or **25%** where they come from residential letting of any kind including tourist lets, reducible for mainly-affordable portfolios (RDL 29/2026, pending convalidation, tax periods open on 8-10-2026); must distribute 100% of dividends received, ≥50% of gains on disposals (rest reinvested within 3 years) and ≥80% of other profits (art. 6).

[en:M1:T11:concepts:5]

- Defaulting owner: can attend the assembly but not vote (while debt persists and is not judicially challenged); loses the vote; and since Law 10/2022 the assembly may adopt deterrent measures for as long as the arrears last — interest above the legal rate or temporary suspension of the use of services or facilities — if not abusive or disproportionate and never affecting habitability (art. 21.1).
- Extinction effects (beyond the two causes already noted): cancellation of independent registry folios per unit, reopening of the parent registry record, settlement of pending community rights/obligations, and distribution of remaining community assets (notably the reserve fund) among owners per their quotas.

- VUT approval within a community (art. 7.3 + 17.12): an owner wanting to run a tourist-use dwelling needs the community's EXPRESS prior approval by 3/5 majority; the community can also approve/restrict/prohibit such activity and set special expense quotas (increase capped at 20%, non-retroactive).

question:
Un hombre es dueño de dos fincas colindantes y pide a su notario que constituya una servidumbre de paso sobre una de ellas a favor de la otra mientras conserva ambas. El notario le dice que no puede constituirse ninguna servidumbre. ¿Qué requisito de la servidumbre falta?
Opciones: inseparable / indivisible / dueños distintos / predial.

Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T17:concepts:3]
Módulo 1 · Tema 17: Real Property Rights (Derechos Reales) — Key concepts
- Use and habitation: more limited than usufruct, STRICTLY PERSONAL — cannot be assigned or leased (unlike usufruct, which can generally be transferred/leased).
- Easement (servidumbre): burden on a servient estate for benefit of a dominant estate (or person); predial easements are inseparable from their estates. Types: of way (paso), of light and view (luces y vistas), of aqueduct, party wall/medianería, altius non tollendi (height restriction).

[en:M1:T23:concepts:8]
Módulo 1 · Tema 23: Mortgage/Registry Law — The Registral Property, First Registration, and Cadastre Coordination — Key concepts
- Charges/encumbrances catalog and registry effect: mortgage (constitutive registration, priority in sale proceeds); judicial/administrative attachment (preventive annotation, art. 42.2 LH, 4 years renewable, binds subsequent acquirers); easement (registered on the SERVIENT estate's folio — apparent easements bind third parties even unregistered — case law; art. 13 LH sets the general rule that charges must be registered to affect third parties); usufruct/use/habitation (reduce bare owner's powers while in force); **explicit resolutory condition (CRE, arts. 1504 CC/11 LH)** — seller reserves the right to rescind a sale for non-payment of deferred price, registered as a charge on the buyer's folio, functionally similar to a mortgage but without the mortgage regime; prohibition on disposal; tax charges (ITP/AJD, IIVTNU/plusvalía) — property remains liable for these for 5 YEARS via a marginal note, and the ACQUIRER answers SUBSIDIARILY, with the property itself, if the tax is not paid (art. 79 LGT); the seller's unpaid IBI likewise charges the property, in subsidiary liability (art. 64 TRLRHL).

- Easement/servidumbre (art. 530 CC): encumbrance on a servient estate for the benefit of a dominant estate belonging to a DIFFERENT owner. Characteristics: indivisible (affects the whole servient estate even if only part is used, art. 535); inseparable (can't be transferred apart from the estate, art. 534); predial (falls on an estate — personal easements are the exception); must be possible; requires "otherness"/alterity — cannot exist between estates of the same owner (nemine res sua servit — usufruct/use rights are NOT easements).

Legality/calificación registral (art. 18 LH): the Registrar reviews extrinsic form, grantors' capacity, substantive validity, and registry obstacles BEFORE registering — outcomes: entry made, suspended (curable defect, deadline given), or denied (incurable) — appealable to DGSJFP/courts. 8. **Tracto sucesivo/successive chain of title (art. 20 LH)**: to register a transfer, the TRANSFEROR's right must already appear registered — an unbroken registered chain. Czworo kuzynów od piętnastu lat jest współwłaścicielami działki, bez żadnej umowy o utrzymaniu niepodzielności. Jedno z nich chce teraz znieść współwłasność i podzielić grunt; pozostała trójka odmawia. Czy może ona teraz żądać podziału?

AJD jest znacznie tańsze niż ITP (konkretne stawki regionalne: Kastylia i León AJD 1,5%, Andaluzja AJD 1,2%). Brak zysku kapitałowego IRPF dla współwłaściciela otrzymującego pieniądze odpowiadające wartości jego udziału (tylko ewentualna nadwyżka jest zyskiem); ustępujący współwłaściciel JEST opodatkowany IIVTNU (gminny podatek od przyrostu/plusvalía) od wzrostu wartości gruntu przypadającego na jego udział.

question: I rent a shop for my business at 8,300 euros a month and want to sublet part of it. What monthly rent can my landlord demand after that?
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T8:concepts:12]
Módulo 1 · Tema 8: Law 29/1994 on Urban Leases (LAU) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Other-use leases (Title III, arts. 29-35): mostly free agreement; art. 32 lets a business/professional tenant sublet/assign WITHOUT landlord consent (contrast with housing leases) but landlord gets a rent increase (10% partial sublease, 20% assignment/full sublease); art. 34 grants compensation to a retail tenant losing the premises after ≥5 years of activity provided the tenant stated, 4 months before expiry, the wish to renew for at least 5 more years at market rent; if the tenant reopens the same business in the same municipality within 6 months, compensation = moving costs + lost clientele; if not, and the landlord or a third party runs the same or a similar business there within 6 months, 1 month's rent per year of the lease (max. 18).

[en:M1:T9:concepts:5]
Módulo 1 · Tema 9: The Lease Contract — Course Module on the LAU (Condensed Practitioner View) — Key concepts
- Deposit (fianza) administrative mechanics: must be LODGED by the landlord with the competent regional housing body within a set period (Castilla y León: Junta de Castilla y León, 30 business days; Andalusia: AVRA — Agencia de Vivienda y Rehabilitación de Andalucía) — separate from the LAU's civil regime of returning it to the tenant. Total guarantee ceiling for habitual-residence leases: deposit (1 month) + additional guarantees (max 2 months) = max 3 months total.
- Comparative snapshot (residential vs. other-use lease): duration (5/7-yr minimum vs. free agreement/no minimum); assignment/subletting (written consent required vs. free if business activity, with 10%/20% rent increase to landlord); deposit (1 month vs. 2 months); rent update (index-capped vs. freely agreed); compensation to tenant on expiry (none for housing vs. available for retail/commercial premises under art. 34).

[en:M2:T24:concepts:2]
Módulo 2 · Tema 24: Business Formation and Contracting — Key concepts
- ERL (limited liability entrepreneur, Ley 14/2013) lets a sole trader shield the habitual residence from business debts only if its value is at most €300,000 (ITP-AJD taxable value when registered in the Commercial Registry; ×1.5 in towns of over 1,000,000 inhabitants) (art. 8.2) — requires notarial deed + registration in Commercial Registry AND Property Registry; debts contracted before registration keep full liability unless the creditor consents (art. 9.3); the shield is lost for later debts if annual accounts are not filed within 7 months of year-end, and regained on filing (art. 11.3); tax and Social Security debts are outside the shield, although the habitual residence can be sold for them only if no other sufficient assets are known and at least 2 years after the first attachment notice (Disposición adicional primera); no protection for fraud/gross negligence.

[en:M1:T8:concepts:11]
Módulo 1 · Tema 8: Law 29/1994 on Urban Leases (LAU) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Termination causes the landlord can invoke ipso iure (art. 27.2): non-payment of rent or agreed amounts, non-payment/non-renewal of deposit, unconsented subletting/assignment, bad-faith damage or unconsented works, unlawful/nuisance activities, dwelling ceasing to serve the tenant's permanent housing need. Tenant can terminate for landlord's failure to repair (art. 21) or landlord interference with use.

[en:M1:T8:vocab:1]
Módulo 1 · Tema 8: Law 29/1994 on Urban Leases (LAU) — Primary Legislative Text — Spanish vocabulary
| arrendamiento urbano | urban lease |
| arrendador / arrendatario | landlord / tenant |
| prórroga forzosa / tácita | compulsory / tacit extension |
| fianza | security deposit |
| desistimiento | withdrawal (from the contract) |
| subrogación | subrogation (succession into the lease) |
| tanteo y retracto | right of first offer and right of redemption |
| gran tenedor | large-scale property holder |
| zona de mercado residencial tensionado | stressed residential market area |
| desahucio | eviction |
| traspaso | transfer of a business premises lease |
| inquilinato | (old term for) residential tenancy |
| renta | rent |
| more uxorio | cohabiting as if married |
answer: Under the LAU, a business tenant may sublet without landlord consent (art. 32), but the landlord may demand a 10% rent increase for partial sublease. The original rent is 8,300 euros. A 10% increase would be 830 euros, making the new rent 9,130 euros. Answer: 9,130 euros.

question:
Carlos bought a country house from a man who, it later turned out, was not its owner; Carlos neither knew nor had any reason to suspect this. For three years he rented the house out. The true owner has now won a court case to recover it. Must Carlos hand over the rents he collected before the lawsuit was filed?
Options: yes / no.
retrieved_material:
Retrieved context:
[en:M1:T19:concepts:5]
Módulo 1 · Tema 19: Possession (La Posesión) — Key concepts
- Effects by good/bad faith on FRUITS: good-faith possessor keeps fruits received while possession isn't legally interrupted (art. 451 CC), must return only fruits pending/received after bad faith begins; bad-faith possessor must hand over ALL fruits received AND fruits the legitimate possessor could have received (fructus percepti + percipiendi) from the START of possession (art. 455 CC). Either type gets reimbursement for fruit-production expenses if defeated.
- Effects on deterioration/loss: good-faith possessor NOT liable unless intentional; bad-faith possessor liable for ALL deterioration/loss, even FORTUITOUS, unless it would have happened anyway under the true owner.

[en:M1:T17:concepts:10]
Módulo 1 · Tema 17: Real Property Rights (Derechos Reales) — Key concepts
- **Actions protecting property — key distinctions**: vindicatory action (acción reivindicatoria — recover possession from a non-titled holder; claimant must prove ownership + defendant's possession + individualized identification; NOT time-barred unless usucapión has already run) vs. declaratory action (claimant already possesses, just wants title formally recognized — not time-barred) vs. negatory action (deny a claimed third-party encumbrance exists — 30-year period) vs. Publician action (protects a possessor mid-usucapión against a weaker-right possessor — case-law recognized, not in the CC) vs. enclosure action (right to fence the property — 30 years) vs. third-party ownership claim/tercería de dominio (stop enforcement against an asset that isn't actually the debtor's — must be brought before the auction).

[en:M1:T11:concepts:4]
Módulo 1 · Tema 11: Horizontal Property — Course Module (Condensed Practitioner View) — Key concepts
- Debt-collection payment-order procedure (proceso monitorio): the initial petition needs no lawyer or procurador whatever the amount (art. 814.2 LEC); if the debtor opposes, they are needed once the claim exceeds €2,000 (arts. 23, 31 and 818 LEC). File with the Court of First Instance: (1) the certificate of the assembly's debt-liquidation resolution, issued by the secretary with the president's approval and stating the amount and its breakdown, and (2) proof that the debt was notified to the debtor (or posted on the community notice board for at least 3 days) (art. 21.3 LPH). If the debtor neither pays nor opposes within 20 days, the monitorio ends and execution is issued on the community's request; suing the registered owner lets the execution reach the flat (art. 816 LEC, art. 21.2 LPH).

[en:M1:T8:concepts:10]
Módulo 1 · Tema 8: Law 29/1994 on Urban Leases (LAU) — Primary Legislative Text — Key concepts
- Landlord's upkeep duty (art. 21): must keep dwelling habitable at no rent increase (except tenant-caused damage); if repairs last >20 days and deprive tenant of part of the dwelling, rent is reduced proportionally. Since 8 Oct 2026, for repairs affecting habitability, safety or health the tenant may send a written request with a reasonable quote; if within 15 calendar days the landlord neither accepts it, proposes an alternative nor does the repair, the tenant may do the works and deduct the cost from future rent (art. 21.5, RDL 29/2026, pending validation by Congress).

[en:M1:T19:vocab:1]

| corpus / animus | material element / intentional element |
| animus domini | intent to hold as owner |
| posesión civilísima | civilísima (constructive/automatic) possession |
| poseedor de buena/mala fe | possessor in good/bad faith |
| frutos percibidos | fruits received |
| gastos necesarios / útiles / de lujo | necessary / useful / luxury expenses |
| derecho de retención | right of retention |
| interdicto posesorio | possessory injunction (historical term) |
| acción publiciana | Publician action |
| despojo | dispossession |
| tradición | delivery |

answer: Módulo 1 · Tema 19: Possession (La Posesión) — Key concepts. Good-faith possessor keeps fruits received while possession isn't legally interrupted (art. 451 CC). Must return only fruits pending/received after bad faith begins. The true owner's claim is a vindicatory action (acción reivindicatoria), which is not time-barred. Carlos, as a good-faith possessor, is not liable for fruits received before the lawsuit. Answer: no.
